definitions.explanation: A channel or ditch running alongside a road or building to carry away rainwater and wastewater.

examples.japanese: {側溝|そっこう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{落|お}ち{葉|ば}→落ち葉：14108_ochiba⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{詰|つ}まっている→詰まる：02079_tsumaru⟧。
examples.english: The drainage ditch is clogged with fallen leaves.

examples.japanese: ⟦{大雨|おおあめ}→大雨：03015_ooame⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧とき、{側溝|そっこう}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧あふれた。
examples.english: During the heavy rain, water overflowed from the roadside gutter.

examples.japanese: ⟦{自転車|じてんしゃ}→自転車：00633_jitensha⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{前輪|ぜんりん}→前輪：28610_zenrin⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{側溝|そっこう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{蓋|ふた}→蓋：03896_futa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{隙間|すきま}→隙間：00389_sukima⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{挟|はさ}まって→挟まる：04668_hasamaru⟧⟦{転倒|てんとう}→転倒：14303_tentou⟧しそうになった。
examples.english: The front wheel of my bicycle got caught in the gap of a gutter cover and I nearly fell over.

notes:
A compound of {側|そく} (side) and {溝|こう} (ditch, channel). Refers to the concrete or stone channels that run along the edges of roads in Japan to drain rainwater.

In Japanese residential areas, {側溝|そっこう} are ubiquitous — nearly every street has them. They are often covered with metal or concrete grates. Bicycle riders in Japan learn to be careful of {側溝|そっこう} grates, as thin tires can get caught in the gaps.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {側溝|そっこう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{蓋|ふた}→蓋：03896_futa⟧: gutter cover, drain cover
- {側溝|そっこう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{掃除|そうじ}→掃除：02889_souji⟧: gutter cleaning
- {側溝|そっこう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{落|お}ちる→落ちる：01242_ochiru⟧: to fall into a ditch
- {側溝|そっこう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{詰|つ}まる→詰まる：02079_tsumaru⟧: for a gutter to become clogged

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{排水溝|はいすいこう}→排水溝：07335_haisuikou⟧: drain, drainage channel — more general term for any drainage outlet
- ⟦{溝|みぞ}→溝：09410_mizo⟧: ditch, groove — everyday word for any channel or groove
- ⟦{用水路|ようすいろ}→用水路：19104_yousuiro⟧: irrigation channel — carries water for agricultural use
